$comment: City lights below a sunset glow on the Earth's edge, square, for the landing page's night-lighting card background, rendered by FOSS Earth with no interface (the website credits Google beside it). The time is the scenes' first instant, 22:16 UTC on 25 October 2026. The observer is on the great circle from São Paulo away from the Sun, where the Sun is 4° below the Earth's edge, in the Earth's shadow. From orbit the meter reads the ground below (sky.exposure.groundMeterAltitude), which is at night, so it exposes for the night and the cities show. Looking 40° right of the Sun makes the glow on the edge run from white to orange to red. The edge sits about a quarter of the way down, so a card's heading and text fall on the dark, lit ground below it. Tune with --set, e.g. --set observer.fromReference.sunAboveLimbDeg=-6, --set camera.headingOffsetDeg=50 or --set settings.renderer.exposureEV=1 (exposure compensation on top of the meter, in stops, + brighter); compare exposures with --bracket=-2,-1,1,2.
name: night-lights-orbit
description: From 400 km over the Atlantic off Espírito Santo at 22:16 UTC on 25 October 2026, looking west-north-west across lit Minas Gerais and Goiás to the sunset glow on the Earth's edge beyond Brasília.
